posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
Eh... I'm not really a fan of puzzles in RPG's, but I'll give you the ones I felt really proud for figuring out and stuck with me.
Final Fantasy 6
The Zozo clock puzzle.  "The clock has stopped, set the time?".  You choose hour, minutes, seconds.  Everyone in Zozo tells you different times.  Gives you different hints.  Except... pretty much all of the hints don't work.  They're contradictory in nature.  So who is right?  When 13 year old me figured out, "Zozo is the town of criminals and outlaws.  Everyone here lies.  The answer is the times they aren't telling me", was one of the best feelings I ever had in video games up to that point.
The game didn't tell me how to solve the puzzle at all.  It just gave a couple worldbuilding facts about the place before I arrived, and everyone there was shady or wanted to fight...  And I just... made the simple deductive leap about the place, to solve the puzzle.
In an age of no internet (or rather, I didn't have access to the internet), this was kind of cool at the time.  Like, the game rewarded my paying attention and thinking about the problem in a more lateral way than most games did at the time.
Pokemon Ruby
The Braille puzzles.  I didn't have internet at the time to solve these instantly for me.  No, I had to painstakingly write down the script I found in the locations (because I didn't find the cipher first), and then figure out how to translate it.  When I found the cipher, I wasn't sure what I was looking at, at first.  But, I kept looking at it, and looking at it, and realized it was basically the alphabet.  So, I wrote the whole thing down, and then applied it to the script of locations I had found earlier.  Now that they were translated, I could finish the puzzle.
Kind of a fun "aha" moment for me.  I translated Braille into written english with the only guidance being a cipher block that doesn't tell you it's the cipher at all, and you get no hints as to what you're looking at.
Was kind of fun at the time.

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
I'm not really a fan of any fishing in RPG's or even most games.  But, here's a weird and yet maybe fun fact for those of you who like fishing in games:
Every game my friend and I play together... we end up fishing together.  The only game we've ever played where we didn't fish together was Ark.  Mostly because it requires sap to do or whatever you use for bait, and we just never went ahead and did it.
If it was multiplayer and had fishing, we went fishing together.  No, I don't know why.  It's just our thing, I guess.
I guess it's easier to tolerate fishing for me when I got a buddy to do it with.  Someone to compare catches with, or have pointless conversations.
I still wish games that had fishing gave you a "mastery" option where you could just chuck explosives in and get fish that way.  Something fun to do when you no longer NEED to fish anymore, but you want to cause a little mayhem or something.
I saw Fallout 76 added fishing recently, too.  I'm sure my friend will drag me into that game again at some point to fish with him.
